properties.statement:
OBSERVED (sinogram trial, 2026-10-27): reasoning_report at budget_chars 6,000 trimmed every prose field to zero.

MEASURED (read-only, design 066be35ae5418abb via the flo2 connector, reflow2 0.92.0, budget_chars 6000): page 1 of 22 claims, the claim req:pred-arcs WHOLE (its `says`, the step's rule and warrant, each premise's name): so reflow2:req:the-reasoning-read-back-keeps-the-words-of-the-claims-it-returns HOLDS. Outside the claim: fields_trimmed 20, prose_limit 0, summary_room 0, what_this_means "…", every assumption/evidence/unsupported name "…", five lists cut to 1 entry (assumptions 1 of 9). budget.reply_chars 9,529 against 6,000; its own note: "EVERY LIST IS AT ITS FLOOR OF ONE ENTRY AND THE REPLY IS STILL 2233 CHARACTERS [over]".

PRECEDENT: reflow2:fact:the-zero-rung-blanks-every-name-over-80-characters-so-a-reasoning-summary-reads-as-dots-2026-10-25: the claims page takes the budget first and leaves the summary 0 room; the 0 rung blanks every string over NEVER_TRIM_BELOW = 80. Options listed, "Not built". At main 983811cae reply_budget.rs line 103 still has NEVER_TRIM_BELOW 80 and query.rs still computes summary_room after the page.

CANDIDATES: (1) the page-first allocation plus the 0 rung (precedent). HOLDS: summary_room 0, prose_limit 0. (2) The budget asked (6,000) is below what one whole claim of this design needs (~7,300 in the claim alone). HOLDS as a contributor: a claim kept whole cannot fit, so the reply must overrun or cut the claim; reflow2 chose to overrun and say so. (3) Outside reflow2: flo2's persona block and wrapper add characters. Contributes about 700 characters, not the 3,500 over. (4) I measured the wrong reply. REFUTED: budget.reply_chars is reflow2's own count.

CLASS: a budget split with no reserve for the summary, and a floor sized for ids applied to names. New beside 10-25: when one whole claim exceeds the budget, the reply exceeds it silently-by-number (reply_chars in the budget block), which reflow2:req:no-reply-grows-with-the-design-each-fills-its-budget-and-says-how-to-read-on's gate would fail.

FIX, ranked: (a) reserve summary room first (names and counts at the 80-char floor, never 0), then fill the claims page; when one claim alone is over the budget, return zero claims plus the summary and `next_offset`, with a note naming the budget a claim needs (keeps both the claims req and the budget); (b) the 10-25 floor fix alone (names cut to 80 plus "…"); (c) raise flo2's default. NOT ESTABLISHED: the trial's own call (its reply was not kept); whether the one gate that requirement asks for (not yet built, as far as read) would call reasoning_report on a design this size. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018ibUbMKCS1yK5W17cncp9P
